general_protocol: General Cross-Project Research Protocol v0.7.4 FINAL
question: When a lower-scale linear mechanical subsystem is reduced to an effective boundary component and then re-embedded into a larger system, which declared higher-level response quantities are preserved exactly, approximately, or poorly across an ordinary coupling/frequency landscape?

native_comparator_context.approximate_comparator_1: Guyan-style static condensation transformed consistently for mass, stiffness, and damping

exact_closure_tests: full inverse outer compliance versus direct one-step Schur elimination
direct one-step Schur elimination versus nested inner-then-boundary Schur elimination
direct group-to-outer return versus nested group-to-outer return
exact_tolerance_role: software/mathematical identity tolerance only; not a physical inheritance threshold

report: relative outer-compliance error across every grid point
relative return/self-energy error across every grid point
frequency and coupling coordinates of maximum error
approximation_reporting.rule: No arbitrary approximation error cutoff will be introduced after inspecting the landscape. Approximate methods remain descriptive P0-D surfaces until a task-specific tolerance is independently justified.

function_map_targets: regions where exact nested closure remains numerically identical to the unreduced system
ordinary regions where approximate reductions closely follow the unreduced higher-level response
how approximation error changes with internal coupling, outer coupling, and frequency
limit_map_targets: frequencies/couplings where static condensation loses higher-level response fidelity
frequencies/couplings where one-mode internal truncation loses higher-level response fidelity
numerical nonidentifiability or singular/ill-conditioned regions if encountered
controls: boundary_outer_coupling=0 control, where the lower subsystem cannot alter the outer response through the removed coupling path
no Atlas coordinate or chi used for parameter selection
